q: 1. The bricks should be burnt at temperature from ............
explain: Bricks must be burnt between 1000°C and 1200°C to achieve vitrification. Below 1000°C, they remain soft; above 1200°C, they may melt and distort.

q: 2. The type of brick suitable for panel walls for multi-storeyed buildings is ............
explain: Both hollow and perforated bricks are used in high-rise panel walls to reduce the dead weight of the structure and provide better thermal insulation.

q: 3. The length of a curved tile varies from ............
explain: Curved or pan tiles used for roofing generally have a standard length ranging from 15 cm to 20 cm as per sunil Sah Book and Geek Mcq But as per google option d .

q: 4. A bull nose brick is not used for ............
explain: Bull nose bricks have rounded corners and are used for aesthetics and safety on pillars or wall ends, but they are not used for structural arches.

q: 5. King closers are related to ............
explain: A king closer is a type of brick cut used in masonry where one corner is cut off so the width at one end is half the full width.

q: 6. Generally wooden moulds are made from ............
explain: Sisham is often preferred over teak because it is generally more affordable while providing excellent longevity and stability, according to IndiaBIX and ZoneTech.

q: 7. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is ............
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous, permanent structure with a roof, allowing brick burning to continue even during the rainy season.

q: 8. The bricks after moulding should be dried in ............
options: air for 3 to 8 days but not in sun
explain: Bricks should be dried in the shade (protected from direct sun) to prevent uneven drying and cracking.

q: 9. The indentation marks left on bricks during the process of moulding, are known as ............
explain: The 'frog' is the depression on the top face of the brick. It serves as a key for mortar and often displays the manufacturer's name.

q: 10. For sanitary pipes and chemical stonewares,
explain: Salt glazing provides a highly resistant, acid-proof, and impermeable surface, making it ideal for pipes carrying sewage or chemicals.

q: 11. The usual percentages of clay and metal in cermet are
explain: Cermets (Ceramic-Metal composites) used in high-temperature applications often contain approximately 80% ceramic (clay/oxide) and 20% metal binder.

q: 12. If the iron ore contains clay as an impurity, the flux added during calcinations is
explain: Limestone ($CaCO_3$) is a basic flux added to react with acidic impurities like clay/silica to form slag that can be easily removed.

q: 13. Sewer pipes are made of ...............
explain: Stoneware is highly resistant to chemical attacks, corrosion, and erosion, making it the ideal material for conveying sewage which contains acids and gases.

q: 14. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is ...............
options: equal to size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of fully burnt brick
greater than the size of fully burnt brick
explain: Bricks shrink during the drying and burning processes. Therefore, the mould must be slightly larger (usually 8-10%) than the required finished size.

q: 15. Pug mill is used for ...............
explain: Pugging is the process of grinding and mixing clay with water to make it plastic and homogeneous, which is performed in a pug mill.

q: 16. The frog of a brick in a brick masonry is generally kept on ...............
explain: The frog (indentation) is kept upward so that it can be filled with mortar, creating a mechanical key between courses for better shear resistance.

q: 17. The shape of the brick gets deformed due to rain water falling on hot brick. This defect is known as ...............
explain: Chuffs are the deformations or cracks caused by the rapid cooling of hot bricks when exposed to falling rain.

q: 18. The percentage of alumina in a good brick clay should vary from ...............
explain: Alumina provides plasticity to the clay. A content of 20-30% is ideal for moulding; excess alumina causes bricks to crack on drying.

q: 19. In continuous flame type kiln, the maximum diameter of the kiln is at ...............
explain: The diameter is usually kept maximum at the mid-height to allow for a better distribution of heat and to facilitate the downward movement of the materials.

q: 20. Glazing of clay products, is done ...............
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing serves multiple purposes: it makes the product impervious to liquids, protects it from weather, and provides a smooth, aesthetic finish.

q: 21. A pug mill is used for ...............
explain: Tempering is the process of bringing the clay to a proper degree of hardness and plasticity by mixing it with water, which is done in a pug mill.

q: 22. To which category do the chromite bricks belong?
explain: Chromite bricks are neutral refractory bricks; they are resistant to both acidic and basic slags and are used in furnaces for various metals.

q: 23. Minimum thickness of wall where single Flemish bond can be used is ...............
options: one and a half brick thick
explain: Single Flemish bond uses Flemish bond for the face and English bond for the backing. It requires at least a 1.5-brick thick wall to accommodate this structural transition.

q: 24. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads is ...............
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brickwork because it has no continuous vertical joints between courses, making it ideal for load-bearing walls.

q: 25. Clay and silt content in a good brick earth must be at least ............
explain: A good brick earth should contain about 50% silica and a combined total of clay and silt around 50% to ensure proper plasticity and strength.

q: 26. When a brick is cut into two halves longitudinally, one part is called ............
explain: A queen closer is a brick piece cut in half along its length, used to close the bond at the end of a course.

q: 27. The red colour obtained by the bricks is due to the presence of ............
explain: Iron oxide in brick earth (usually 5-6%) imparts the characteristic red color to the bricks upon burning.

q: 28. Hollow bricks are generally used with the purpose of ............
explain: The air trapped inside hollow bricks acts as an excellent thermal insulator, keeping the building cool in summer and warm in winter.

q: 29. The frog of the brick is normally made on its .............
explain: The 'frog' is an indentation made on the top face of a brick to form a key for the mortar and to reduce the weight of the brick.

q: 30. The weight of a good quality brick when immersed in water for a period of 16 hours should not exceed the weight of dry brick ............
explain: A standard first-class brick should not absorb more than 20% of its dry weight in water, ensuring it is dense and durable.

q: 31. The percentage of alumina in a good brick earth lies between ............
explain: A desirable brick earth contains 20-30% Alumina. Too little reduces plasticity; too much causes cracking during drying.

q: 32. The portion of the brick without a triangular corner equal to half the width and half the length is called
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting off a triangular corner from one end, such that the cut width is half the original width and the cut length is half the original length.

q: 33. Bricks produced by washing the inside surface of the brick mould with water are known as ...
explain: Slop moulding involves wetting the mold with water to prevent the clay from sticking, resulting in a smoother finish than sand moulding.

q: 34. The size of modular bricks, is ............
explain: The standard or modular size of a brick is 19 cm x 9 cm x 9 cm; when mortar joints are included, it becomes 20 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm.

q: 35. Bricks manufactured by clearing the inside surface of the brick mould with sand are known as ............
explain: In sand moulding, sand is sprinkled on the inner sides of the mould to prevent the wet clay from sticking to it.

q: 36. Machine moulding of bricks can be done by ............
explain: Industrial brick manufacturing uses both plastic clay (wire-cut) machines and dry-press machines depending on the moisture content of the clay.
